purpose: RESEARCH_LOG #16 left a loose end. qlib158/vstd60 is a WEIGHTED member of the frozen twelve (0.0960, direction +1), labelled a 60-day volume-stability measure, and the paired VWAP re-test's side diagnostic showed it crushed by a plain 20-session realised-vol sort at ranking tail risk (5.27 vs 12.76 pp on validation h=1). The vendor formula is ts_std(volume,60)/volume, whose denominator is TODAY's volume rather than the 60-day mean, so the quantity is not a coefficient of variation and moves inversely with current volume. This audit asks only what vstd60 actually correlates with cross-sectionally. It is the same class of question the VWAP basis defect turned out to be: is a factor measuring what its label claims.

preregisteredHypothesis.claim: vstd60 ranks 60-day volume STABILITY, as its label and its use in the frozen twelve assume
preregisteredHypothesis.falsifiedIf: cross-sectional rank correlation with inverse current volume exceeds that with a true 60-day coefficient of variation, on both windows

knownLimitations: A correlation audit says what a factor co-moves with, never whether it predicts returns. No edge, no promotion and no weight change can follow from this file.
Both evaluation windows have already been viewed, so this run can reject a labelling claim but cannot establish anything tradeable.
#12 already showed the frozen twelve carry no day-neutral selection edge at any horizon, which caps what any single-factor finding here can mean for the book.
Spearman correlation on a single session is sensitive to the eligible-universe composition that day; the day-clustered t over sessions is the reported statistic, not any single day.

volume is backward adjusted in this panel. Ratios of volume to its own trailing statistics are invariant to a per-symbol rescaling, which is what makes this comparison valid, but absolute volume levels are not comparable across symbols.
